title: CPR (Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation)
summary: Immediate emergency resuscitation for cardiac arrest and unresponsive victims.
subtitle: Cardiac arrest emergency
steps: Check responsiveness by tapping the shoulders firmly and shouting loudly.
Call emergency services (112 or 108) immediately and ask for an AED.
Check for normal breathing or chest rise for no more than 10 seconds.
Place heel of one hand in center of chest, other hand on top with interlocked fingers.
Push hard and fast at 100–120 compressions per minute at 5–6 cm depth.
Do not interrupt compressions until emergency medical help takes over or AED arrives.
whenToCall: Call 112 or 108 immediately if the person is unresponsive, unconscious, or not breathing normally.
disclaimer: Not a substitute for professional medical care. In an emergency, always call 112 or 108 immediately.

title: Choking (Adult & Child)
summary: Emergency airway clearance for a conscious choking person unable to breathe.
subtitle: Blocked airway emergency
steps: Ask 'Are you choking?' and encourage coughing if they are able to cough or speak.
If unable to cough or breathe, lean them forward supporting their chest.
Deliver 5 firm back blows between shoulder blades using the heel of your hand.
If airway remains blocked, give 5 quick upward abdominal thrusts (Heimlich maneuver).
For infants under 1 year, alternate 5 back slaps with 2-finger chest thrusts only.
If the victim becomes unresponsive, lower to the ground and start CPR immediately.
whenToCall: Call 112 or 108 immediately if the obstruction does not clear within two cycles, or if the person becomes unresponsive.
disclaimer: Not a substitute for professional medical care. In an emergency, always call 112 or 108 immediately.

title: Severe Bleeding
summary: Rapid hemorrhage control to prevent life-threatening shock.
subtitle: Severe wound hemorrhage
steps: Protect yourself with clean gloves or a waterproof barrier if available.
Apply firm, continuous direct pressure with sterile gauze or clean cloth directly over wound.
Keep pressure constant for at least 5 minutes without lifting the cloth to check.
If blood soaks through, add additional pads on top without removing original dressing.
Elevate the injured limb above heart level only if no broken bones are suspected.
If limb bleeding is uncontrollable, apply a commercial tourniquet 5–7 cm above the wound.
whenToCall: Call 112 or 108 immediately if bleeding spurts, will not stop after 5 minutes of direct pressure, or signs of shock appear.
disclaimer: Not a substitute for professional medical care. In an emergency, always call 112 or 108 immediately.

title: Burns (Thermal & Chemical)
summary: Immediate cooling and protective care for thermal, chemical, or electrical burn injuries.
subtitle: Heat or chemical burn
steps: Ensure personal scene safety and safely remove the heat source or chemical exposure.
Cool the burn under clean, cool running water for at least 20 minutes.
Gently remove rings, watches, and restrictive clothing before swelling develops.
Do NOT apply ice, butter, oils, toothpaste, or adhesive bandages to burned skin.
Loosely cover burned skin with a sterile non-stick dressing or clean plastic wrap.
Keep the person warm to prevent hypothermia during prolonged cooling.
whenToCall: Call 112 or 108 immediately for burns larger than the palm, burns on face/airway/joints, electrical burns, or chemical exposure.
disclaimer: Not a substitute for professional medical care. In an emergency, always call 112 or 108 immediately.

title: Fracture & Sprains
summary: Safe immobilization and trauma management for suspected bone or joint fractures.
subtitle: Bone and joint injury
steps: Instruct the injured person to remain completely still and avoid moving the injured area.
Support the injured limb in the exact position found without attempting realignment.
Never attempt to straighten a deformed limb or push an exposed bone back into flesh.
Control any open wound bleeding with gentle pressure around the wound, avoiding the bone.
Apply an ice pack wrapped in a cloth for 15 minutes at a time to reduce swelling.
Immobilize with a splint only if transport is unavoidable and you are properly trained.
whenToCall: Call 112 or 108 immediately if bone pierces the skin, limb is cold or blue, or head, neck, or spine injury is suspected.
disclaimer: Not a substitute for professional medical care. In an emergency, always call 112 or 108 immediately.

title: Snake Bite
summary: Crucial immobilization protocol for venomous snake puncture injuries.
subtitle: Venomous puncture wound
steps: Keep the patient calm, lying down, and completely still to slow venom circulation.
Remove rings, bangles, watches, and shoes immediately before rapid limb swelling occurs.
Immobilize the bitten limb at or slightly below heart level with a splint.
Apply a firm crepe pressure bandage from extremities toward torso if trained.
Do NOT cut the wound, suck out venom, apply ice, or tie a tight arterial tourniquet.
Note the snake's color and markings safely, and transport immediately to hospital.
whenToCall: Call 112 or 108 immediately for any venomous snake bite or puncture wound with swelling, pain, or dizziness.
disclaimer: Not a substitute for professional medical care. In an emergency, always call 112 or 108 immediately.

title: Drowning & Flood Rescue
summary: Safe water extrication and emergency resuscitation for submersion victims.
subtitle: Water submersion emergency
steps: Ensure rescuer safety first; reach or throw a floating object, do not enter dangerous water.
Remove victim from water safely while supporting their head and neck.
Check responsiveness and normal breathing immediately once on dry ground.
If not breathing, deliver 5 initial rescue breaths followed by 30 chest compressions (CPR).
Continue cycles of 30 chest compressions and 2 rescue breaths until help takes over.
If breathing normally, place in recovery position on their side and keep warm.
whenToCall: Call 112 or 108 immediately for any submersion incident, even if the person appears to recover quickly.
disclaimer: Not a substitute for professional medical care. In an emergency, always call 112 or 108 immediately.

title: Heat Stroke
summary: Emergency rapid whole-body cooling for life-threatening hyperthermia.
subtitle: Dangerous core overheating
steps: Move the person immediately into dense shade or an air-conditioned room or vehicle.
Remove heavy outer clothing to expose as much skin surface as possible.
Rapidly cool the person by spraying cool water while actively fanning their skin.
Apply cold wet cloths or ice packs to the neck, armpits, and groin.
Do NOT force fluids if the person is confused, drowsy, vomiting, or unconscious.
Monitor breathing and consciousness closely until emergency medical teams arrive.
whenToCall: Call 112 or 108 immediately. Heat stroke (temperature over 40°C, confusion, rapid pulse) is an extreme medical emergency.
disclaimer: Not a substitute for professional medical care. In an emergency, always call 112 or 108 immediately.

title: Fainting (Syncope)
summary: Emergency management for temporary loss of consciousness due to reduced brain blood flow.
subtitle: Temporary loss of consciousness
steps: Lay the person flat on their back on the ground immediately.
Elevate their feet and legs 20–30 cm above heart level to restore blood flow to brain.
Loosen tight collars, ties, belts, or restrictive clothing around the neck.
Ensure fresh airflow by opening windows and asking onlookers to step back.
If they do not regain consciousness within 1 minute, roll into recovery position and check breathing.
Do not allow them to stand up quickly once awake; have them rest lying down for 10 minutes.
whenToCall: Call 112 or 108 immediately if the person remains unconscious for over 1 minute, has chest pain, or fell and struck their head.
disclaimer: Not a substitute for professional medical care. In an emergency, always call 112 or 108 immediately.

title: Poisoning & Ingestion
summary: Immediate toxicity response for ingested chemicals, pesticides, or toxic substances.
subtitle: Toxic chemical exposure
steps: Ensure personal safety and remove the victim from toxic fumes or chemical contact area.
Safely identify the toxic container, chemical label, plant, or medication involved.
Do NOT induce vomiting unless specifically instructed by poison control or emergency doctors.
If the substance is on skin or in eyes, flush continuously with clean water for 15 minutes.
If unconscious but breathing normally, place in the recovery position on their side.
Bring the chemical container or substance sample with the patient to the hospital.
whenToCall: Call 112 or 108 immediately, or call the National Poison Information Centre (1800-116-117) with the product details.
disclaimer: Not a substitute for professional medical care. In an emergency, always call 112 or 108 immediately.
